passage:
An old weather station on a mountain had recorded temperature and rainfall for many decades. Its instruments looked simple compared with modern satellites.
A scientist told students that long records are extremely valuable. They help researchers see changes over time.
The station had survived storms, repairs, and budget cuts because local workers cared for it.
Students realized that important science can depend on routine. Someone had to climb the mountain, check instruments, and write numbers again and again.
Big conclusions often rest on small repeated actions. A graph may look clean, but behind it are years of patient work.
